summary: Waldur 8.1.5-rc.4 makes the Arrow billing integration safer and more predictable. Each license-month is now billed once, invoices that are already issued are never changed, an overcharge and an API key exposure are fixed, and staff can preview billing changes in a wizard before applying them. Site-agent offerings can now store their agent configuration in Waldur, checked against the plugin catalogue, and Waldur builds the agent's config file from it. A token wizard with a site-agent template, service accounts and the OFFERING.MANAGE_AGENT and OFFERING.UPDATE_AGENT_CONFIGURATION permissions support this. Marketplace changes include an order flow diagram for each offering, component limits that can only be increased, category sections and attributes that can be edited from the UI, and resource API keys revealed via POST. Proposal calls gain Excel exports, messages to reviewers, decline reasons for reviews, and a call event feed hidden from reviewers. Events can now be deleted after a configurable retention period, settable from Helm and Docker Compose. The previous month's invoices now stay open for 2 hours by default. The release also adds a feedback survey wizard, MCP connection guidance and an AI inference micro-app, and fixes several OpenStack, metrics and usage-reporting issues.

entries.title: Accept the typed confirmation of RabbitMQ delete all and purge all
entries.description: The typed confirmation for the RabbitMQ delete all and purge all actions was not accepted. It now is.

entries.title: Ask about volumes and floating IPs when batch-terminating instances
entries.description: Previously, batch-terminating instances did not ask about their volumes and floating IPs. Now, the batch terminate dialog asks how to handle them.

entries.title: Build the Mastermind image in two stages
entries.description: Previously, the Mastermind image was built in a single stage. Now, it is built in two stages, and the build checks the resulting runtime image.

entries.title: Check a resource request against the offering's components when it is made
entries.description: Previously, a proposal's resource request was checked against the offering's components only at allocation. Now, it is checked when the request is made, so a request that does not match the offering's components is refused up front.

entries.title: Choose what guards an automatic allocation decision
entries.description: Previously, an automatic allocation decision could not rely on the provider fulfilling each order. Now, a call manager chooses what guards an automatic allocation decision step, and can let it rely on the provider fulfilling each resulting order. Workflow checks, descriptions and reports reflect the chosen guard.

actions.description: Proposal migration 0101_callworkflowstep_automatic_decision_guard adds the guard to workflow steps.

entries.title: Declare who may call every API endpoint
entries.description: Previously, the proposal endpoints and five other endpoints in social auth, marketplace, promotions and Rancher did not declare who may call them. Now, they do, and service provider team management is described as owners may perform it.

entries.title: Disable the proposal checklist-template route, which could only fail
entries.description: The proposal checklist-template API route could only fail. It is disabled.

entries.title: Email a configured address when a new Waldur release is available
entries.description: Previously, Waldur did not email anyone when a new release became available. Now, a scheduled task emails a configured address when a new Waldur release is available.

actions.description: Core migration 0055_versionupdatenotification adds the version update notification model.
Set the recipient address for release notifications in the configuration settings to receive these emails.

entries.title: Email reviewers when an onboarding justification is submitted
entries.description: Previously, reviewers were not emailed when an onboarding justification was submitted. Now, they receive an email when one is submitted.

entries.title: Enforce personal access token bindings and external-only sharing in OpenStack networking
entries.description: Previously, a personal access token was not held to its bindings when creating ports, in the network owner checks or at a router's gateway. A port, instance or router interface could also be put on a network shared only as external. Now, these operations respect the token's bindings, networks shared only as external refuse ports, instances and router interfaces, and the remaining port interface gaps are closed.

security.affected_versions: 8.1.4 and earlier (first affected release not identified in the commit data)
security.exploitability: Requires an authenticated user who either uses a personal access token bound to narrower scopes or has access to a network shared with their tenant only as external.

entries.title: Expose offering documentation and support links in assistant discovery tools
entries.description: Previously, the assistant's offering discovery tools did not expose documentation and support links, and a search that matched nothing did not say why. Now, the tools include an offering's documentation and support links, including for the anonymous persona, and a search that matches nothing names the unmet requirement.

entries.title: Fill event message placeholders only from event context and escape their values
entries.description: Previously, placeholders in event message templates could be filled from text that people wrote, and the values put into the templates were not escaped. Now, placeholders are filled only from the event context, inserted values are escaped, and tests check that event messages across core, marketplace, invoices, policy, proposals, support and the OpenStack plugin follow this.

security.affected_versions: 8.1.4 and earlier (first affected release not identified in the commit data)
security.exploitability: Requires an authenticated user who can write text that ends up in an event message. Placeholders in that text could be filled from the event context, and its values were inserted without escaping.

entries.title: Fix login alert, user details, team dialog, tab and brand colour issues
entries.description: The login error alert layout was broken, and the roles table did not fit in the user details dialog. The one-project-manager check was not refreshed after a team change. Tab counts did not follow the active tab, embedded tabs did not keep the tallest tab's height, and the ToS row and reviewer profile divider were misdrawn. Custom brand buttons could get a lighter hover than their default colour (brands darker than 0.4 lightness) or a darker 500 step than the brand itself (brands lighter than 0.55). All are fixed, and brand steps now scale from the brand's own lightness where a fixed value would flip their order. Brands near 0.4, including the default green, are unchanged.

entries.title: Gate the demo preset API behind a deployment setting
entries.description: Previously, the demo preset API had no deployment-level switch. Now, it is available only when the deployment enables it through a setting, exposed in Helm as waldur.demoPresets and passed to Mastermind by docker-compose.

actions.description: To use demo presets, enable them in the deployment: set waldur.demoPresets in Helm values, or the demo preset variables in docker-compose's .env.

entries.title: Import fractional prices given as numbers exactly
entries.description: Fractional prices given as numbers in an offering import were not imported exactly. They now are.

entries.title: Invoice prepaid renewals at their quote
entries.description: Prepaid renewals were not invoiced at the price quoted for the renewal. They are now invoiced at their quote.

entries.title: Keep per-run task state out of the shared task object
entries.description: Background tasks kept per-run state on the shared task object. That state is now kept per run.

entries.title: Keep the Resource model in the generated Python client
entries.description: The generated Python client was missing the Resource model. OpenAPI schema generation now keeps it, and CI checks Python SDK generation.

entries.title: Let call organisers read the reviewer profiles of the pools they manage
entries.description: Previously, call organisers could not read the profiles of reviewers in the pools they manage. Now, they can, and the reviewer profile is shown when a call team or reviewer pool row is expanded.

entries.title: Limit how many active proposals an applicant may hold with a call-managing organisation
entries.description: Previously, an applicant could hold any number of proposals with a call-managing organisation at once. Now, a call-managing organisation can limit how many active proposals an applicant may hold with it at once, set from the organisation's call manager panel.

actions.description: Proposal migration 0098_callmanagingorganisation_max_active_proposals adds the limit field.

entries.title: Limit table filters to values that have rows using backend facets
entries.description: Previously, table filters offered every possible value. Now, marketplace, proposal and support list endpoints return filter facets, and frontend tables use them to offer only values that have rows. Filter menus also fit short option lists.

entries.title: List the API keys of all a service provider's offerings
entries.description: Previously, a service provider could not list API keys across all its offerings. Now, a provider page lists the API keys of all its offerings, with filters and a summary. Provider resource lists show API key counts, each key carries an estimated cost, and a resource API key's description can be shown and edited.

actions.description: Marketplace migration 0326_resource_api_key_estimated_cost adds the estimated cost to resource API keys.

entries.title: List the deployment's micro-apps in the quick shortcuts menu
entries.description: Previously, the quick shortcuts menu did not list micro-apps. Now, a new feature lists the micro-apps deployed with the frontend in the quick shortcuts menu on desktop and mobile.

entries.title: Log an unreachable remote Waldur during offering pull
entries.description: Previously, an unreachable remote Waldur was not logged during offering pull. Now, pulling offerings from a remote Waldur logs when the remote cannot be reached.

entries.title: Log the real error on port and router sync and import Neutron ports with null fields
entries.description: Port and router sync did not log the real error, and Neutron ports with null fields were not imported. Sync now logs the real error and imports such ports.

entries.title: Make the user management API timeout configurable
entries.description: Previously, the timeout for requests to the user management API, which course accounts and service accounts use, could not be configured. Now, a deployment setting sets it, with documented bounds. Helm exposes it in its values, and docker-compose exposes it as WALDUR_USER_MANAGEMENT_API_TIMEOUT.

actions.description: Optionally set WALDUR_USER_MANAGEMENT_API_TIMEOUT in docker-compose, or the corresponding Helm value, to change the timeout.

entries.title: Move the frontend from Bootstrap to Tailwind and shared waldur-ui components
entries.description: Previously, the frontend depended on Bootstrap, hand-rolled tables, separate stat tiles and static inline styles. Now, Bootstrap is removed, and the frontend uses Tailwind and shared waldur-ui components throughout. These cover tables, stat cards, number inputs, attachments and upload zones, code blocks, expandable rows and Matrix chat components. Form fields and buttons follow a named control height scale, dialog footer actions have a width floor and size to their label, row status colours come from tokens, and table density lost during the migration is restored.

entries.title: Move the reviewer registry and feedback surveys under Support
entries.description: Previously, the reviewer registry and feedback surveys were managed from the administration. Now, the reviewer registry is under Support > User management, and feedback surveys are under Support > Communication.

entries.title: Name the projects and resources created by a call's accepted proposals
entries.description: Previously, a call could not name the projects and resources its accepted proposals create. Now, a call manager can set a project name template on the call, and the projects and resources created for accepted proposals are named from it. Applicants see a preview of the resulting project name when they create a proposal.

actions.description: Proposal migration 0100_call_project_name_template adds the naming template fields.

entries.title: Polish marketplace, resource, reporting and tab layouts
entries.description: Previously, several screens had inconsistent actions, tabs and card states. Now, pending consumer order actions sit in a three-dots menu, and Access resource is the main action in the resource header. A tab bar holding a single tab is hidden, and the category page drops its header and titles the offerings block with the category. Offering page tabs use shared components, organization tab counts appear as tab counts, and expandable-row tabs size to their tallest tab. Clickable cards share hover, pressed and focus states, and report card headers, user analytics charts and maintenance report filters are aligned.

entries.title: Polish the call administration, award and review screens
entries.description: Previously, several call management screens had layout and wording issues. Now, the call administration screens have team badges, a read-only Add action, and clearer toasts, header and texts, with Crossref spelled as the vendor spells it. Award screens show budget names, the differs flag and an award edit warning. A proposal count of one uses singular wording, and the proposal runs table sits flush in its section. The award change badge stays whole beside long offering names, and linked stat cards are clickable. Assignment batches list their proposals in the standard table, and Open validation stays on the workflow check's line. Round settings are edited in plain dialogs, with the allocation edit disabled when there is no date.

entries.title: Preview and load demo presets from the administration
entries.description: Previously, demo presets could not be previewed or loaded from the administration. Now, staff can preview a demo preset's contents and load it from the administration. A preset loads in the background while the API is paused and a reset overlay is shown. Loading keeps deployment-owned settings, resets the rest and turns on the features each preset's demo needs. A deployment can add its own presets, an overlay and a staff password, which docker-compose mounts and passes through. The login page offers quick login for demo users.

actions.description: Marketplace migration 0325_demo_preset_load adds demo preset load tracking.

entries.title: Provider calls micro-app with post-award work told apart from award orders
entries.description: Previously, a service provider's post-award work and its award orders were not told apart. Now, the API tells them apart, and a new provider calls micro-app, built on a shared waldur-proposals package, covers a provider's inbox, requests, proposals, demand, team work and awards. It handles purchase-order awards, offers actions only where the provider's permissions allow them, and links to the relevant sections.

entries.title: Record the impersonator behind a policy evaluation for staff and support only
entries.description: Previously, policy evaluation events did not record the impersonating user in a place that only staff and support can read. Now, the impersonator behind a policy evaluation is recorded there.

entries.title: Refuse checklist answers that reference a stored file uploaded elsewhere
entries.description: Previously, a checklist answer could name a stored file that had been uploaded elsewhere. Now, such an answer is refused.

security.affected_versions: 8.1.4 and earlier (first affected release not identified in the commit data)
security.exploitability: Requires an authenticated user who can answer a checklist and knows the reference of a stored file uploaded elsewhere. The answer could then point at that file.

entries.title: Refuse frontend API requests with an unfilled path parameter
entries.description: The frontend API client could send a request with an unfilled path parameter. It now refuses such requests.

entries.title: Remove the invoice item consumptions action, which always failed
entries.description: The invoice item consumptions API action always failed. It is removed.

entries.title: Remove the unused SLURM PRIVATE_KEY_PATH setting and SSH key mounts
entries.description: Previously, Mastermind had an unused SLURM PRIVATE_KEY_PATH setting, and Helm and docker-compose provided and mounted an SSH key pair for it. Now, the setting, the Helm SSH key values, secret, config map and mounts, and the docker-compose id_rsa mounts are removed.

actions.description: Drop SSH key values from custom Helm values and the id_rsa files from docker-compose configuration. They are no longer used.

entries.title: Rename and describe a plan that resources use
entries.description: Previously, a plan used by resources could not be renamed or have its description changed. Now, it can, and the plan form keeps the billing period of a plan in use unchanged.

entries.title: Render the proposal PDF on the server
entries.description: Previously, the proposal PDF was built in the browser with pdfmake. Now, the server renders it and includes only what the requesting reader may read, and the frontend downloads it from the server.

entries.title: Require signed SAML2 logout requests from the session's identity provider
entries.description: Previously, SAML2 logout requests were accepted without requiring a signature from the identity provider of the user's session. Now, a logout request must be signed by that identity provider.

security.affected_versions: 8.1.4 and earlier (first affected release not identified in the commit data)
security.exploitability: A logout request that was unsigned or came from another identity provider could end a user's Waldur session.
security.mitigation: Upgrade to 8.1.5-rc.1 or later, and confirm that identity providers sign their logout requests, because unsigned ones are now refused.

entries.title: Restrict call reviewer pools, organisation statistics, offering dependents and reviewer bids to authorized users
entries.description: Previously, a call's reviewer pool was shown beyond those who manage its review. A call-managing organisation's statistics were shown beyond those who may read its reports, what depends on an offering was shown to users who may not change it, and a reviewer's bid could be changed or withdrawn by someone other than that reviewer. Now, each is limited to the users who hold that right. The frontend hides the reviewer pool from users who may not read it, and opens the call list instead of the dashboard for organisation owners without a call role.

security.affected_versions: 8.1.4 and earlier (first affected release not identified in the commit data)
security.exploitability: Requires an authenticated user with some access to a call, a call-managing organisation or an offering.

entries.title: Run calls for proposals on configurable workflows with call templates and validation
entries.description: Previously, calls for proposals did not run on configurable workflows. Now, each call runs on a configurable workflow of steps and can be created from one of 21 bundled call templates, such as rapid, regular, beamtime, NAIRR and AI Factory access. Before use, the workflow can be validated, described and dry-run, and it adds new workflow notification emails. Call managers can add the award response step by its key right after the allocation decision, give and take a call team's reviewer role, and edit project details fields through edit buttons. Checklists offer an organization only when calls use them as forms, and staff manage call templates from the administration.

actions.description: Proposal migrations 0092-0097 move existing calls onto workflows (expand, backfill, contract), delete empty proposal documents and backfill review submission times.
Checklist migration 0017 adds an organization to checklists, and configuration migration 0004 drops removed reporting screens.

entries.title: Save only their own fields in resource write-back actions
entries.description: Resource write-back actions saved more than their own fields, so concurrent changes to other fields could be overwritten. They now save only their own fields.

entries.title: Serve the chat tool registry over MCP with an OAuth consent bridge
entries.description: Previously, the MCP server was built on fastmcp and did not serve the chat tool registry. Now, it uses the official mcp SDK, serves the chat tool registry acting as the calling user, and adds an OAuth consent bridge API. MCP events have their own labelled event group.

entries.title: Set a logo for a call for proposals
entries.description: Previously, a call for proposals was shown with its initials. Now, call managers can set a logo for a call. The logo is shown in place of the initials on call cards and the call's pages, and can be edited there.

actions.description: Proposal migration 0099_call_image adds the call logo field.

entries.title: Show a resource's usage and limit for the whole order period
entries.description: Previously, a resource's usage was not available for the whole order period. Now, the API exposes a resource's usage for the whole order period, and the resource details show usage and limit for that period, governed by an offering resource display option.

entries.title: Show files attached to step answers by name and size with download links
entries.description: Files attached to workflow step answers were shown as a raw dictionary. They are now shown by name and size and offered as download links, including in project metadata answers.

entries.title: Show Matrix chat mentions, unread counts and notification levels in Waldur
entries.description: Previously, the chat welcome and role notice did not wait for room members to join, and chat mentions, unread counts and notification levels were not shown inside Waldur. Now, a room's welcome and role notice are posted once its members have joined. Waldur shows chat mentions, an unread count (including in the page title) and notification levels.

actions.description: Matrix chat migration 0014_matrixroom_announced_at records when a room was announced.

entries.title: Show offering and service provider managers the plans of their offerings
entries.description: Offering managers and service provider managers could not see the plans of their offerings. The plans list now includes them.

entries.title: Show private OpenStack volume types only to those who may use them
entries.description: Private OpenStack volume types were shown to users who could not use them. Volume types now record whether they are public, and private ones are shown only to those who may use them.

actions.description: OpenStack migration 0091_volume_type_is_public adds the public flag to volume types.

entries.title: Show round awards and awarded project teams to call managers and results readers
entries.description: Previously, the managing organisation's results readers could not see the award of a published round, and a call manager could not list the team of a project that the call's award created. Now, both can. When the project access of an allocation outcome cannot be loaded, the proposal view explains why.

entries.title: Show what an extension asks for, carried out and skipped
entries.description: Previously, the proposal views did not show what an approved extension carried out or skipped, and the state of a resource an extension skipped was not named in plain words. Now, the post-award section shows what an approved extension carried out and what it skipped, with the skipped resource's state named in plain words. The offering assessment card shows what an extension asks of the offering.

entries.title: Show which settings the deployment manages
entries.description: Previously, the administration did not show which settings the deployment manages. Now, the administration settings, service desk, identity provider, language and Matrix admin screens mark the settings that the deployment manages.

entries.title: Skip resources younger than the window in the stale-resource reminder
entries.description: The stale-resource reminder included resources younger than its window. It now skips them.

entries.title: Stop matching accounts by an email address their user set
entries.description: Previously, sign-in and SCIM matching could find an existing account by an email address that the account's own user had set. Now, an email address a user set themselves is never used to find an account at sign-in or in SCIM matching, and the email lookups for invitations and OpenPortal access apply the same rule.

security.affected_versions: 8.1.4 and earlier (first affected release not identified in the commit data)
security.exploitability: Requires an account whose user can set its own email address. If that user sets it to another person's address, the account could be matched when the other person signs in or is matched over SCIM.

entries.title: Switch between accounting and billing mode with a feature flag
entries.description: Previously, accounting and billing mode could not be switched with a feature flag. Now, a billing mode feature flag switches the UI between them, adjusting organization cost columns, invoice and billing views, invoice printing, price tooltips and the revenue growth chart.

entries.title: Upgrade gunicorn from 22.0.0 to 26.2.0
entries.description: Previously, Mastermind ran on gunicorn 22.0.0. Now, it runs on gunicorn 26.2.0, with the bundled gunicorn.conf.py updated for it.

entries.title: Upgrade oauthlib to 4.0.1 for GHSA-3jp2-3mrg-2vxc
entries.description: The bundled oauthlib dependency is upgraded to 4.0.1 to address GHSA-3jp2-3mrg-2vxc.

security.affected_versions: Waldur releases bundling oauthlib older than 4.0.1, up to and including 8.1.4
security.exploitability: See GHSA-3jp2-3mrg-2vxc. The commit data does not state whether Waldur's use of oauthlib is exposed.

entries.title: Validate an edited pending order as its creation was validated
entries.description: Previously, editing a pending marketplace order skipped validation that was applied when the order was created, including personal access token bindings. Now, an edited pending order goes through the same checks as its creation, including in the OpenPortal order processors.

security.affected_versions: 8.1.4 and earlier (first affected release not identified in the commit data)
security.exploitability: Requires a user who can edit a pending order. The edit could carry values that creation-time validation would have refused.

entries.title: Clearer detail views for Identity Bridge, onboarding and provider calls
entries.description: Previously, the user's Identity Bridge tab and onboarding application details used a denser layout, and provider calls had no state column of their own. Now, the Identity Bridge tab and onboarding details are shown as plain key/value sections, and provider calls have their own state column and a sectioned expanded row.

entries.title: Content-Security-Policy on API responses, HTML pages and error pages
entries.description: Previously, some API responses, mastermind's own HTML pages, and error pages generated by gunicorn, the web shell and the reverse proxies were served without a Content-Security-Policy. Now, every API response carries a policy, and mastermind's HTML pages carry a page policy. The SAML logout page no longer names an IPv6 address as a source. Gunicorn, the web shell, the Helm ingresses and the Docker Compose Caddy proxy send a policy on their own error pages. The homeport image sends a complete policy for the portal, and both Helm and Docker Compose now take the portal's policy from the image. In Docker Compose, Caddy also sends a policy on any response that lacks one and closes connections for unknown hosts.

actions.description: Review custom Content-Security-Policy settings in Helm values or the Docker Compose environment: the portal's policy now comes from the homeport image (see the Helm content-security-policy documentation).

entries.title: customer.billing_mode feature renamed to customer.show_invoices_with_vat
entries.description: Previously, the feature that controls how invoices are presented was called customer.billing_mode. Now, it is called customer.show_invoices_with_vat. A migration renames the stored feature, the portal reads the invoice presentation from the new name, and the Helm chart maps the billing feature to it. Docker Compose drops the unused homeport config.template.json.

actions.description: Apply core migration 0059_rename_billing_mode_feature, which renames the stored feature.
Update any configuration overrides or scripts that set customer.billing_mode to use customer.show_invoices_with_vat.

entries.title: Demo preset loading and demo user sign-in
entries.description: Previously, loading a demo preset broke Waldur's links to Matrix accounts and rooms, demo preset support users did not get the deployment's staff password, and the login page listed demo users. Now, the Matrix links survive a preset load, support users get the staff password too, and the login page no longer lists demo users because they sign in through the demo identity provider.

entries.title: Idempotent credit top-ups with recorded channel
entries.description: Previously, a repeated top-up request could be applied more than once, and the channel a top-up came through was not recorded. Now, top-ups are idempotent and each credit transaction stores its channel, which can be used to filter transactions.

actions.description: Apply invoices migration 0038_credit_transaction_channel.

entries.title: Invoices page gated on INVOICE.LIST permission
entries.description: Previously, the portal did not check the INVOICE.LIST permission before showing the Invoices page. Now, the page and its navigation tab are shown only to users with that permission.

entries.title: Lock accounts instead of whole addresses after failed password sign-ins
entries.description: Previously, repeated failed password sign-ins locked out the whole source address. Now, the lockout applies to the affected account, so other users signing in from the same address are not blocked.

entries.title: Map validated OIDC ID-token claims to user attributes
entries.description: Previously, user attributes could not be taken from claims in a validated OIDC ID token. Now, these claims can be mapped to user attributes. The identity provider forms in the portal explain where each claim comes from and warn when the email claim is unverified.

entries.title: No hardcoded default for AI_ASSISTANT_MODEL
entries.description: Previously, AI_ASSISTANT_MODEL had a hardcoded default model. Now, the default is gone, so the model must be set explicitly.

actions.description: Deployments that use the AI assistant and relied on the default model should set AI_ASSISTANT_MODEL explicitly.

entries.title: Number inputs accept typing, show errors and keep decimals
entries.description: Some number inputs could not be typed into, hid validation errors or dropped decimals. This affected component multipliers, the options form, total limit tables, plan quotas, order field editing and the what-if simulator. These inputs now accept typing, show their errors and keep decimals.

entries.title: Permission required to reveal shared resource API keys
entries.description: Previously, any role with access to a shared resource API key could reveal it, including when calling with an access token. Now, revealing it requires a dedicated reveal permission and requests made with access tokens are refused. The portal disables Reveal for roles without the permission and lists the permission in role and personal access token scope options. The Request API key dialog now makes choosing the project key an explicit choice.

actions.description: Apply permissions migration 0039_reveal_api_key_permission.
Review custom roles that need to reveal shared resource API keys and grant them the new reveal permission.

entries.title: Portal layout and display fixes
entries.description:
Fixes several display issues in the portal:
- The chat icon's unread dot now counts live encrypted messages.
- Header notification dots no longer blink.
- Long login button labels wrap instead of overflowing.
- Inline controls stay transparent in an unavailable offering's view.
- The refresh button stays on the resource name line.
- The table selection bar sits beside the search box instead of being centred.
- Paged tables keep their tallest page's height so pagination does not move.
- Termination dates are formatted in every resource list.
- The offering partition edit dialog's submit button is labelled Save.

entries.title: Project digest notification switch honoured
entries.description: Project digests ignored the project digest notification switch, and a test digest that was not sent gave no feedback. Digests now honour the switch, the API reports when a test digest was not sent, and the project digest settings page warns about it. A migration updates the project digest notification setting.

actions.description: Apply structure migration 0089_enable_project_digest_notification.

entries.title: Public service provider page no longer crashes without a provider record
entries.description: The public service provider details page crashed when the provider had no provider record. The page now renders in that case.

entries.title: Resource-ending mail follows the offering's reminder schedule
entries.description: Previously, the mail warning that a resource is ending did not follow the offering's reminder schedule. Now, it is sent on that schedule.

entries.title: Settings commands and docs named after the settings store
entries.description: Previously, the commands for dumping and overriding settings were named after Constance (dump_constance_settings, override_constance_settings). Now, the commands and documentation are named after the settings store (dump_settings, override_settings), and the bundled init-whitelabeling and matrix-init scripts are updated to match.

actions.description: Review custom scripts that call dump_constance_settings or override_constance_settings and switch them to dump_settings and override_settings.

entries.title: Shared CPU software builds named after their target machine
entries.description: Previously, shared CPU builds in software catalogs were not labelled by the machine they target. Now, they are named after the machine they were built for.

entries.title: Step-up re-authentication for sensitive account changes
entries.description: Previously, a signed-in session could change token lifetime, email address, passkeys and personal access tokens, or widen a personal access token's allowed networks, without confirming the user's identity again. Now, these changes require step-up re-authentication, and the portal shows a dialog asking the user to confirm it is them before the change goes through. Pending email change requests are deleted by a migration.

actions.description: Apply the core migrations 0056_reauthentication, 0057_delete_pending_email_change_requests and 0058_reauthentication_widen_pat_networks, and the passkeys migrations 0003_reauthentication and 0004_reauthentication_widen_pat_networks.
Pending email change requests are deleted on upgrade; users with an unfinished email change must request it again.

entries.title: Token scopes applied to end date and limit change requests
entries.description: Token scopes were not applied when filing project end date, resource end date and resource limit change requests. Waldur now applies them to these requests.

entries.title: Activating an offering's ToS version deactivates the active one
entries.description: Previously, activating another Terms of Service version did not deactivate the active one. Now, it does, and the UI warns about this when a version is added or edited.

entries.title: AI assistant charts monthly costs for organizations and projects
entries.description: Previously, the assistant could not chart costs. Now, a chart_costs tool draws incurred cost and credit/compensation per month as stacked bars, ending with an estimate for the current month. It follows the same access rules as the REST endpoints. The monthly figures come from invoices.utils.monthly_costs, which /api/invoice-items/costs/ now also uses, so the two match. Text taken from user data is cut to the chart limits instead of the chart being dropped, untitled plots keep their chart, and a period with no costs is reported as such.

entries.title: AI assistant prompt includes portal and user context
entries.description: Previously, the assistant's prompt did not describe the portal or the user, and the persona carried the date and currency, so it changed daily. Now, a platform block follows the shared part of the prompt. It holds the date, currency, site description, public service categories, what the portal offers, and the conceal_prices, catalogue_only and call_only rules. A user block follows with the user's organizations and projects and their roles, including projects visible through an organization role and excluding terminated ones. Names are quoted and normalized so they cannot pose as prompt entries. The prompt tells the assistant to treat the project list as background, not something to report.

entries.title: AI assistant proposal tools limited to what the caller may see
entries.description: The AI assistant's proposal tools could show more than the caller was allowed to see. They now return only the applicant details that the call shows its reviewers, and give a provider only its own part of a proposal.

entries.title: AI assistant quick prompts chosen by the backend for each user
entries.description: Previously, an empty thread showed six fixed quick prompts, several of which led nowhere. Now, GET /api/chat/suggestions/ returns the prompts to offer. A prompt is offered only when the caller's tool set and the deployment configuration allow it and, for some prompts, when the user has the relevant data, such as a paused resource, pending reviews, a draft proposal, a pending order, credit or an HPC allocation. Staff see only their own prompts. Ordering and review prompts are hidden where the portal has those features off, and a cost chart prompt appears only where the caller may see costs and prices are shown. The UI shows five prompts with a More suggestions toggle and caches the list per user and impersonator.

entries.title: AI assistant searches the Waldur documentation
entries.description: Previously, the AI assistant could not consult the documentation. Now, it searches a bundled docs corpus, filtered by the user's role and the site configuration. Search matches the questions each section answers, gives concept sections more weight, searches in English, and falls back to sections matching any word when too few match every word. Results link to the versioned docs pages, and they name features that are switched off on the site so the assistant can say they are not enabled. The search is also served over REST without the AI assistant. Staff can turn it off with DOCS_SEARCH_ENABLED, which also hides the Search docs suggestion. Release images ship the corpus of their own tag. A bad or unreadable corpus no longer stops a deploy, and lines containing NUL characters are skipped. The ai_assistant command can score docs search and docs answers per role and site state.

actions.description: Migrations 0021_docsection and 0022_docsection_kind_context add the documentation section table and its fields.

entries.title: AI assistant settings split into topic tabs
entries.description: Previously, the AI assistant settings were shown as one list. Now, they are grouped into topic fieldsets and shown as tabs on the settings page.

entries.title: AI assistant streams model reasoning and shows a single status line
entries.description: Previously, model reasoning was not streamed to the AI assistant. Now, reasoning is streamed and shown in a single status line while the assistant thinks. <think> tags are stripped from answers for anonymous visitors.

entries.title: API schema fixes for the Python client
entries.description: The Python client could not parse project permissions, imported projects or the quickstart offerings, and returned None for several response bodies. The API schema and serializers are fixed, and response bodies are now declared. Projects with an invalid kind are reset to the default kind.

actions.description: Migration structure 0090_project_invalid_kind_to_default resets projects with an invalid kind to the default kind.

entries.title: Award membership and OpenPortal shortname rules enforced
entries.description: Previously, local team changes on award projects were not checked against the award's membership rules, and OpenPortal user shortnames were not validated. Now, award membership rules are enforced on local team changes. Shortname rules are enforced, users can set their own shortname, and changes are pushed to OpenPortal.

actions.description: Migration 0040_alter_userinfo_shortname updates the shortname field.

entries.title: Background pulls stopped for inactive service settings and terminated tenants
entries.description: Background pulls kept running for inactive service settings and terminated tenants. They are now skipped.

entries.title: Break a metric figure down by several attributes at once
entries.description: Previously, a metric figure could be broken down by only one attribute. Now, it can be broken down by several attributes at once.

entries.title: Browse and manage S3 buckets from a storage resource
entries.description: Previously, users had to work with S3 storage resources through an external S3 client. Now, S3 storage resources have a Buckets tab. Users can list, create and inspect buckets and objects, delete folders, and get S3 client setup instructions. The backend handles these requests through the resource's API key with a built-in S3 client and request signer, and records the actions as events.

entries.title: Call options for supporting documents, project descriptions and submission checks
entries.description: Previously, a call could not require supporting documents or set the description of the projects it creates. Now, a call can require a minimum number of supporting documents, and it can set a template for the description of projects created from its accepted proposals. Apps can also register checks that a proposal must pass before it is submitted.

actions.description: Migrations 0106_call_project_description_template and 0107_callproposalfieldconfig_minimum_supporting_documents add the new call fields.

entries.title: Checklist completion counts only the questions shown
entries.description: Checklist completion counted questions that were hidden by the answers given. Completion now counts only the questions shown, and existing completions are recalculated. In the UI, dependencies on multi-select answers are now compared by value.

actions.description: Data migrations checklist 0018_recompute_completion_visible_questions and proposal 0103_recompute_checklist_completion_visible_questions recalculate existing checklist completions.

entries.title: Close open reviews and assignments when reviewers leave or proposals are decided
entries.description: Previously, pending reviews and assignments stayed open after a reviewer was revoked or left the call's pool, or after the proposal was decided. Now, a reviewer's pending assignments close whenever they leave the pool, and the applicant is concealed from assigned readers. A proposal's open reviews and assignments close when the proposal is decided, with a new 'proposal decided' rejection cause. The reviewer's pool entry is locked before an assignment is accepted, to prevent races.

actions.description: Migration 0102_close_assignments_of_departed_reviewers closes existing pending assignments of reviewers who have already left a call's pool. Migration 0108_review_rejection_cause_proposal_decided adds the new rejection cause.

entries.title: Create manual assignment batches from a CSV
entries.description: Previously, manual assignment batches had to be built by hand. Now, they can be created from a CSV of proposal IDs and reviewer emails.

entries.title: Dark-theme login logo with LOGIN_LOGO_DARK
entries.description: Previously, the login page used the same logo in light and dark themes. Now, the new LOGIN_LOGO_DARK setting provides a logo that is shown on the login page in dark mode. Separately, the default hero image now appears only when no image has been uploaded.

entries.title: Delegated AI assistant sessions offered only the tools they may run
entries.description: The prompt's tool catalog, search_tools and the canned rejection computed the tool set without the delegation flag. As a result, an impersonating staff member or a token-authenticated session could see and load the HPC tools, and every call to them then failed with a permission error. The delegation flag is now applied everywhere the tool set is computed.

entries.title: Docker Compose: Keycloak bumped to 26.8.2 for CVE fixes
entries.description: The bundled Keycloak is bumped to 26.8.2 for CVE fixes, and its healthcheck is fixed. RabbitMQ, tuwunel and LiveKit receive patch bumps.

security.affected_versions: Docker Compose deployments that run the bundled Keycloak before 26.8.2
security.exploitability: The commit names CVE fixes in Keycloak but not the specific identifiers; exposure depends on whether the bundled Keycloak is used and reachable.
security.mitigation: Pull the updated docker-compose configuration and recreate the Keycloak container.

entries.title: Docker Compose production hardening
entries.description: Previously, the Compose setup trusted forwarded addresses loosely, recommended chmod 666 on the Docker socket, and did not rotate container logs. Now, Caddy keeps a load balancer's X-Forwarded-For entries and sends Waldur only the client address resolved from trusted proxies. DOCKER_GROUP_ID replaces the chmod 666 advice, and every container's Docker log is rotated. The passkey and read-only database settings are passed to the mastermind containers. The README covers mounting the terms of service and privacy policy, running a release tag, upgrading with local changes, and removing the Docker socket mount when script offerings are unused.

actions.description: Set DOCKER_GROUP_ID instead of making the Docker socket world-writable. After setting TRUSTED_PROXY_COUNT, restart the mastermind services.

entries.title: Escape spreadsheet formulas in exports and names in chart tooltips
entries.description: CSV and clipboard exports did not escape spreadsheet formulas, and chart tooltips did not escape names. Exported values that start a spreadsheet formula are now escaped, and names in reporting, usage, aggregate-limit and OpenPortal chart tooltips are escaped.

security.exploitability: Requires a user who can set a name or text value that another user later views in a chart tooltip or opens in a spreadsheet after export.
security.mitigation: Upgrade to 8.1.5-rc.3. Until then, take care when opening exported CSV files in spreadsheet applications.

entries.title: Faster user lists through cached identity provider lookups
entries.description: Previously, user lists looked up identity providers four times per user. Now, each identity provider is looked up once per user list.

entries.title: Fewer queries in the SLURM periodic policy sync
entries.description: Previously, the SLURM periodic sync queried an offering's limit period repeatedly. Now, it queries it once per policy.

entries.title: Filter projects by start and end date, active period and grace period
entries.description: Previously, projects could not be filtered by their dates. Now, the project list can be filtered by start and end date, by active period, and by grace period.

entries.title: Go-live configuration defects fixed in image settings and initdb
entries.description: The image settings, metadata and the load_user_agreements command contained configuration defects found during go-live review. These are fixed.

entries.title: Helm: bundled Postgres, RabbitMQ, tuwunel and LiveKit bumped
entries.description: Previously, the chart bundled older versions of these services. Now, it bundles Postgres 17.12, RabbitMQ 4.3.8, tuwunel v1.9.4 and LiveKit v1.13.11.

entries.title: Helm: HPA, backup secrets and proxy trust fixed for production
entries.description: The Helm chart had defects in HPA, backup storage secrets and trusted proxy configuration that affected production deployments. These are fixed. The fix also updates cronjob image pull secrets and host aliases, the SAML2 secret, and database replica configuration.

entries.title: HPC workspace and AI assistant offer only software that runs on the partition
entries.description: Previously, the HPC workspace and the AI assistant could offer software that does not run on the selected partition. Now, they offer only software that runs on it.

entries.title: Invalid or reused OIDC state sends the user to the login-failed page
entries.description: A sign-in with an invalid or already used OIDC state was not handled gracefully. It now redirects to the login-failed page.

entries.title: Marketplace UI fixes
entries.description: Bulk VM start, stop and restart were disabled for owners who are not staff, and offering, offering edit and order pages failed when no plugin matched the offering type. The inference playground offered models that cannot chat. Owners can now use the bulk actions, those pages render, and the playground offers only chat models.

entries.title: MCP server applies a statement timeout and answers CORS itself
entries.description: Previously, MCP database work had no time limit, and requests to /mcp/ were redirected. Now, a statement timeout bounds MCP database work. /mcp/ is served without a redirect, and the MCP server answers CORS requests itself.

entries.title: Notification fixes for plain-text emails and template editing
entries.description: Plain-text notification emails contained runs of blank lines, and the notification editor did not show the default text or save edits that matched another template. Blank lines are now collapsed, the default text is shown, and such edits are saved.

entries.title: OAuth sign-in and connected apps for MCP clients
entries.description: Previously, MCP clients could not get access through OAuth. Now, the MCP server accepts OAuth tokens and shows OAuth callers only read-only tools. Users approve a client on a consent page, which makes clear that the client acts on the user's behalf. Users can see their connected apps and revoke them from their profile.

actions.description: The new mcp app adds its first migration (0001_connectedapp), which creates the connected apps table.

entries.title: OpenPortal award credit and usage counted per award attachment
entries.description: A project's credit was the current award's allocation minus every invoice item the project ever had. As a result, spend under an earlier award was deducted, which could drive the credit and the derived OpenPortal limits to zero. Total usage looked only at the award's current project, so usage on earlier projects was lost and another award's usage could be counted. Waldur now records when each award is attached to which project, with at most one open attachment per award. Credit, total usage, and usage and storage reports are now counted per attachment, across every project the award was attached to.

actions.description: Migration 0041_managedprojectattachment adds award attachment records, and 0042_backfill_managedprojectattachment fills them in for existing awards.

entries.title: OpenPortal award synchronization fixes
entries.description: This release fixes several issues in OpenPortal award synchronization. Award projects are now named after the local portal, follow corrected identifiers, and stay current when an award moves. Resent awards no longer create duplicate audit entries. An award's links and a project's start date are kept when an update leaves them out. A member outside allowed_domains no longer breaks the remote project list. Code paths that crashed on missing config or missing OpenPortal APIs are fixed. Credit reconciliation is recorded as an adjustment and unchanged credit is no longer rewritten. Project templates return each offering's URL, and userinfo/projectinfo path parameters are typed as UUIDs.

entries.title: OpenPortal award updates applied to live projects; only allocation increases held for review
entries.description: Previously, award updates were not applied directly to live projects. Now, updates from the awarding portal apply to live projects, and only allocation increases are held for review.

actions.description: Migration 0044_managedproject_allocation_review adds allocation review fields to managed projects.

entries.title: OpenPortal project update sent as a registered notification
entries.description: Previously, the OpenPortal project update was not a registered notification. Now, it is sent as a registered, site-neutral notification with editable templates, and it takes the project's grace period into account.

actions.description: Migration 0043_enable_project_usage_update_notification enables the new notification.

entries.title: OpenPortal UI fixes for managed projects, reports and allowed domains
entries.description: This release fixes managed project notes, deletion from the detail page, and string role mappings. The managed projects list gains search and working column sorting. The project usage report now renders when a name mapping is missing and treats storage as a snapshot. Awards that allow no domains are shown as such, and the allowed-domains dialog can lift the restriction. Check user access stays on the page and shows single-user results. Chart tooltips stay inside the chart. Stale report cache entries are purged and evicted when storage is full. Report tabs and Remote Projects pages follow the standard layout.

entries.title: Optional waldur-mcp deployment for Helm and Docker Compose
entries.description: Previously, neither deployment method ran the MCP server. Now, the Helm chart can deploy waldur-mcp with its own service, network policy, ingress or HTTPRoute, and OAuth routes. Docker Compose gains an optional mcp profile with Caddy routes. In both, the MCP server handles CORS on /mcp and its metadata. The Compose service runs read-only, without capabilities, in its own group rather than the Docker socket's, and receives only the credentials it reads. The README documents which images support MCP OAuth sign-in and adds the mcp profile to the upgrade instructions.

entries.title: Project end date handling around the grace period
entries.description: A project's end date could not be changed inside its grace period, the UI did not count end dates to the last usable day, and credit events were projected past the end of the project. The end date can now be changed during the grace period, end dates count to the last usable day, and credit events stop at the project's end.

entries.title: Python dependencies bumped to clear OSV scan findings
entries.description: Previously, the OSV scan reported findings for dnspython, opentelemetry-api and soupsieve. Now, these dependencies are bumped to versions that clear the findings.

entries.title: Resizable and dockable drawers; layout follows the page width
entries.description: Previously, drawers had fixed widths, and page content was laid out by the window's width. Now, drawers can be resized by dragging their edge, the AI assistant drawer can dock beside the page, and header drawers open floating with a common minimum width. The Support drawer's table and search fit its width. Page content, including the proposal page, is laid out by the page's width rather than the window's.

entries.title: Resources provisioned from an award get their resource options
entries.description: Resources provisioned from an award did not have their resource options set. The options are now set.

entries.title: Reviewer-facing proposal UI fixes
entries.description: Previously, star scores appeared for reviews that had not been submitted, My reviews tabs used different headers, and reviewers and panel members could not open the organization view from the Organizations list. Now, star scores appear only for submitted reviews, every My reviews tab has the same header, and reviewers and panel members can open the organization view.

entries.title: Reviewers see only their own reviews in protected rounds
entries.description: In protected rounds, reviewers could see other reviewers' reviews of a proposal. They now see only their own, both in the proposal API and in the AI assistant's proposal tools.

entries.title: Setting changes logged to the system log
entries.description: Previously, setting changes were not written to the system log, and the admin event group was offered. Now, setting changes are logged to the system log, and the admin event group is no longer offered.

entries.title: Software catalogs that are used or not refreshed kept out of retention cleanup
entries.description: Retention cleanup could remove software catalogs that offerings use or that no task refreshes. Such catalogs are now kept.

entries.title: Table, export and app bootstrap fixes
entries.description: Table columns that appeared after the table mounted were not shown, Excel exports became unreadable when text held control characters, and the app bootstrap ran on every window focus. These columns are now shown, Excel exports stay readable, and the bootstrap runs once per page load.

entries.title: Tracked Matrix discussions for call workflow steps
entries.description: Previously, workflow steps had no discussion space of their own. Now, a call manager can give a workflow step a tracked Matrix discussion, and the step's people can open it from the proposal, round and My reviews pages. Apps can define who belongs in the Matrix room for their own kind of scope.

actions.description: Proposal migrations 0104_step_discussions and 0105_step_discussion_constraints_without_nulls_distinct add step discussions.

entries.title: UI consistency polish across dialogs and pages
entries.description: Previously, several dialogs and pages used their own layouts. Now, plan details, change limits and order component tables use the standard dialog table, and plan details appear as a property list. The getting-started dialog groups resources under project tabs with clickable cards. The version history modal and the accounting month cards follow the app's patterns, and the current organization tabs are highlighted. HPC Insights tab hints are inline. Selects and date fields share the input's states. Smaller fixes cover profile tab counts, offering attribute alignment, the empty roles table, the usage history filter width, and the order list and proposals pages.

entries.title: Zero component limits billed and enforced as zero
entries.description: A component limit of zero was not billed and enforced as zero. It now is, in renewal billing and in usage limit restrictions.

entries.title: A quiet usage reporter no longer looks disconnected
entries.description: A site agent that sent usage reports only rarely was shown as disconnected in the integration status. It is no longer shown as disconnected for that reason.

entries.title: Agent configuration for site-agent offerings
entries.description: Previously, a site-agent offering's settings were stored with its other offering settings, and the agent configuration was assembled outside Waldur. Now, each site-agent offering stores its own agent configuration, checked against the vendored site agent plugin catalogue, and existing site agent settings are moved into it. Waldur generates the complete site agent config from this configuration and serves it to the agent as JSON. Changing where an agent connects and what it runs requires the new OFFERING.UPDATE_AGENT_CONFIGURATION permission. A site agent token with OFFERING.MANAGE_AGENT can read its offering's configuration. Service providers edit the configuration in the offering's integration settings.

actions.description: Apply marketplace migrations 0327_offering_agent_configuration and 0328_move_site_agent_settings_to_agent_configuration. 0328 moves existing site agent settings into the new agent configuration.
Apply permissions migration 0040_agent_configuration_permission, which adds OFFERING.UPDATE_AGENT_CONFIGURATION.
Check which roles should hold OFFERING.UPDATE_AGENT_CONFIGURATION.

entries.title: AI assistant tools tested for proposal data leaks
entries.description: Previously, no tests checked whether AI assistant tools leaked proposal data. Now, every AI assistant tool, including docs search and the cost chart, is tested with planted values to confirm it does not leak proposal data.

entries.title: AI inference micro-app
entries.description: Previously, homeport had no AI inference app. Now, an AI inference micro-app adds overview, models, keys, usage and add-service pages, built on a shared charts package.

entries.title: Arrow admin Resources tab and consumption tools reworked
entries.description: Previously, the Arrow Resources tab listed resources from all offerings, and consumption cleanup and force import were not scoped. Now, the Resources tab shows only resources of mapped offerings, has a license column, explains consumption history, and shows a resource's invoice items. Force import is limited to resources of mapped offerings. Consumption cleanup runs from a wizard with a scope and a preview.

entries.title: Arrow admin UI fixes for export type, filters, errors and customer mapping
entries.description: Several Arrow admin UI problems are fixed: the export type in the wizard, search and filters, and error messages. Editing a customer mapping now sends the customer URL and closes when Cancel is clicked.

entries.title: Arrow billing overcharge and unsynced linked licenses fixed
entries.description: Arrow billing could overcharge because line totals were billed more than once, and licenses linked to resources were not synced. Line totals are now billed once and linked licenses are synced. Historical consumption is now looked up by the Arrow license rather than the resource backend_id.

actions.description: Apply waldur_arrow migration 0008_bill_arrow_line_totals_once.

entries.title: Arrow bills each license-month once and never changes issued invoices
entries.description: Previously, Arrow consumption could reach invoices from more than one billing source and could change invoices that were already issued. Now, each Arrow license-month is billed exactly once, issued invoices are never changed, and adjustment items are named after the month they correct.

actions.description: Apply waldur_arrow migration 0009_single_arrow_billing_source.

entries.title: Arrow integration no longer exposes the Arrow API key
entries.description: The Arrow integration exposed the Arrow API key. This release fixes that exposure.

security.affected_versions: Waldur versions before 8.1.5-rc.4 that run the Arrow integration
security.exploitability: The commit data does not describe how the key was exposed or who could read it.
security.mitigation: Upgrade to 8.1.5-rc.4. Consider rotating the Arrow API key.

actions.description: Consider rotating the Arrow API key configured in Waldur.

entries.title: Call event feed hidden from reviewers and panel members
entries.description: A call's reviewers and panel members could see the call's event feed. The feed is now hidden from them.

entries.title: Call managers can message the reviewers of selected proposals
entries.description: Previously, call managers could not message the reviewers of selected proposals from Waldur. Now, they can, and a new event type and notification template support it.

entries.title: Category sections and attributes editable from the Categories admin page
entries.description: Previously, editing category sections and attributes through the API could lose data, and the admin UI had no editor for them. Now, sections and attributes can be edited through the API without data loss, and from the Categories admin page. Public offering pages render the updated sections and attributes.

entries.title: Clearing fields in update dialogs takes effect
entries.description: When a field was cleared in an update dialog, the dialog did not send an explicit empty value, so the clear could fail to take effect. Update dialogs now send explicit empty values. Clearing both fields of a checklist question's onboarding mapping now removes the mapping.

entries.title: Configurable event retention period
entries.description: Previously, events were kept forever. Now, events older than a configurable retention period are deleted by a scheduled task. Operators set WALDUR_EVENT_RETENTION_DAYS through Helm values or the Docker Compose environment. Leaving it empty or setting it to 0 keeps events forever, which is the default.

actions.description: Optionally set WALDUR_EVENT_RETENTION_DAYS (Helm value or Docker Compose .env) to delete events older than the given number of days. Empty or 0 keeps events forever.

entries.title: Dates formatted consistently in one date locale
entries.description: Previously, some dates were formatted with the browser locale or ad hoc tokens. Now, dates are formatted with Intl presets in a single app date locale. This includes the S3 object lock date.

entries.title: Feedback surveys and their questions authored in one wizard
entries.description: Previously, a feedback survey and its questions were created separately. Now, a single wizard covers survey details, audience and schedule, and questions. Questions can be copied from existing surveys.

entries.title: Helm pins postgres-minio and uvk-everypay images and pulls them on every start
entries.description: Previously, these images were not pinned to specific versions. Now, the Helm chart pins the postgres-minio backup image to 17 (rebuilt weekly in place) and uvk-everypay and its sidecar to release 0.2.0. Both are pulled on every run or start.

entries.title: Identity Bridge leaves existing privileged accounts unchanged for non-staff callers
entries.description: When a non-staff caller pushed an existing privileged account to the Identity Bridge, the account was not left as it was. The Identity Bridge now returns the existing privileged account unchanged.

entries.title: Increase-only component limits
entries.description: Previously, customers could lower a component's limit after ordering. Now, a service provider can mark a component's limit as increase-only, which prevents lowering it after ordering. The setting appears in the offering component dialog, is enforced in the change-limits dialogs, and is included in offering export and import.

actions.description: Apply marketplace migration 0329_offeringcomponent_limit_increase_only.

entries.title: Invoice items without an offering component show their own name
entries.description: An invoice item with no offering component was not shown under its own name in the invoice details. It now shows its own name.

entries.title: Keyboard-accessible icon tooltips and tidier property display
entries.description: Previously, some icon tooltips could not be reached with the keyboard, and single properties were wrapped in a one-item list. Now, the remaining icon tooltips are keyboard accessible, and single properties render on their own.

entries.title: Longhorn removal request links to its resource
entries.description: Previously, the Longhorn removal request did not link to the resource it concerns. Now, it does.

entries.title: MCP OAuth accepts CIMD clients that list extra grant types
entries.description: MCP OAuth rejected Client ID Metadata Document (CIMD) clients that listed extra grant types. These clients are now accepted.

entries.title: MCP server URLs in public settings and an AI client connection guide
entries.description: Previously, users had no guidance on connecting an AI client to Waldur's MCP server. Now, MCP server URLs are exposed in public settings, and the Connected apps tab shows how to connect an AI client.

entries.title: Metrics hide resources and projects the caller cannot see
entries.description: Metric reads could include resources and projects the caller cannot see, and the provider side did not follow the same rules as usage. Metric reads now hide those resources and projects, and the provider side follows the usage rules. Hidden metrics show an empty state instead of "Not found".

entries.title: Offering order flow diagram, and the order start date honoured everywhere
entries.description: Previously, there was no overview of how an offering's orders are approved and processed, and the order start date was not honoured on every processing path. Now, the API describes an offering's order flow, and the offering's Actions menu shows it as a swimlane diagram that can be exported. The order start date is honoured on every path.

entries.title: OpenStack tenant orders accept zero cores, RAM and storage limits
entries.description: OpenStack tenant orders rejected limits of zero for cores, RAM and storage. Zero is now accepted for these limits.

entries.title: OS security updates applied in the mastermind and homeport images
entries.description: Previously, the images used their base images' packages as shipped. Now, the mastermind image applies Debian security updates on top of the Python base image, and the homeport image applies Alpine security updates on top of the nginx base image.

entries.title: Preview Arrow billing changes before applying them
entries.description: Previously, staff could not see what Arrow billing actions would change before running them. Now, a Billing changes wizard in the Arrow admin previews invoice changes, and staff apply them only after reviewing them. Billing changes jobs have a total order.

actions.description: Apply waldur_arrow migrations 0010_arrow_billing_changes_job and 0011_arrow_billing_changes_job_total_order.

entries.title: Previous month's invoices stay open for 2 hours by default
entries.description: Previously, the previous month's invoices had a different default grace period, and the Helm chart always set the value itself. Now, they stay open for 2 hours by default. The Helm chart sets the grace period only when an operator configures it, and otherwise uses the mastermind default. The past-month usage rule now also applies to per-user usage reports.

entries.title: Proposal and review exports as Excel workbooks
entries.description: Previously, a call's proposal and review exports were not offered as Excel workbooks. Now, they can be downloaded as Excel workbooks.

entries.title: Resource API keys revealed with POST, and through a token with RESOURCE.REVEAL_API_KEY
entries.description: Now, resource API keys are revealed with a POST request. A personal access token that carries the RESOURCE.REVEAL_API_KEY permission can reveal them.

actions.description: Apply permissions migration 0039_reveal_api_key_permission.
Update API clients that reveal resource API keys to use POST.

entries.title: Reviewers give a reason when sending back an accepted review
entries.description: Previously, a reviewer could send back an accepted review without giving a reason. Now, the reviewer can say why, and the call's managers are notified with that reason.

actions.description: Apply proposal migration 0109_review_decline_reason.

entries.title: SLURM policy options shown only for site-agent offerings
entries.description: Previously, the SLURM lifecycle policy options also appeared on offerings that do not use the site agent. Now, they are shown only for site-agent offerings.

entries.title: SSH port for an offering's SCIM login nodes
entries.description: Previously, an offering's SCIM login node details did not include an SSH port. Now, the SSH port is exposed and can be set in the offering's user management settings.

entries.title: Staff can accept an invitation for a verified user whose email differs
entries.description: Previously, an invitation could not be accepted for a user whose verified email differed from the invited address. Now, staff can accept such an invitation on the user's behalf.

entries.title: Terminated resources counted over the same usage period as active ones
entries.description: Terminated resources were counted over a different usage period than active resources. Both are now counted over the same period.

entries.title: Theme switch moved back into the account menu
entries.description: Previously, the theme switch was in the application header. Now, it is back in the account menu.

entries.title: Token wizard with a site-agent template, service accounts and OFFERING.MANAGE_AGENT
entries.description: Previously, personal access tokens were created in a single dialog, and a site agent needed broader permissions to run. Now, tokens are created in a wizard that includes a site-agent template. A site agent can run with the OFFERING.MANAGE_AGENT permission, and users can be marked as service accounts. Owners of a service provider organization are offered the Create agent token action.

actions.description: Apply core migration 0060_user_is_service_account.

entries.title: User data access log cleanup is scheduled
entries.description: Previously, the user data access log cleanup was not scheduled. Now, it runs as a scheduled Celery task.

entries.title: Volumes of an imported instance take the OpenStack volume state
entries.description: When an OpenStack instance was imported, its volumes did not get the state of the matching OpenStack volume. They now take the state of the OpenStack volume.

since_previous.title: A quiet usage reporter no longer looks disconnected
since_previous.description: A site agent that sent usage reports only rarely was shown as disconnected in the integration status. It is no longer shown as disconnected for that reason.

since_previous.title: Agent configuration for site-agent offerings
since_previous.description: Previously, a site-agent offering's settings were stored with its other offering settings, and the agent configuration was assembled outside Waldur. Now, each site-agent offering stores its own agent configuration, checked against the vendored site agent plugin catalogue, and existing site agent settings are moved into it. Waldur generates the complete site agent config from this configuration and serves it to the agent as JSON. Changing where an agent connects and what it runs requires the new OFFERING.UPDATE_AGENT_CONFIGURATION permission. A site agent token with OFFERING.MANAGE_AGENT can read its offering's configuration. Service providers edit the configuration in the offering's integration settings.

actions.description: Apply marketplace migrations 0327_offering_agent_configuration and 0328_move_site_agent_settings_to_agent_configuration. 0328 moves existing site agent settings into the new agent configuration.
Apply permissions migration 0040_agent_configuration_permission, which adds OFFERING.UPDATE_AGENT_CONFIGURATION.
Check which roles should hold OFFERING.UPDATE_AGENT_CONFIGURATION.

since_previous.title: AI assistant tools tested for proposal data leaks
since_previous.description: Previously, no tests checked whether AI assistant tools leaked proposal data. Now, every AI assistant tool, including docs search and the cost chart, is tested with planted values to confirm it does not leak proposal data.

since_previous.title: AI inference micro-app
since_previous.description: Previously, homeport had no AI inference app. Now, an AI inference micro-app adds overview, models, keys, usage and add-service pages, built on a shared charts package.

since_previous.title: Arrow admin Resources tab and consumption tools reworked
since_previous.description: Previously, the Arrow Resources tab listed resources from all offerings, and consumption cleanup and force import were not scoped. Now, the Resources tab shows only resources of mapped offerings, has a license column, explains consumption history, and shows a resource's invoice items. Force import is limited to resources of mapped offerings. Consumption cleanup runs from a wizard with a scope and a preview.

since_previous.title: Arrow admin UI fixes for export type, filters, errors and customer mapping
since_previous.description: Several Arrow admin UI problems are fixed: the export type in the wizard, search and filters, and error messages. Editing a customer mapping now sends the customer URL and closes when Cancel is clicked.

since_previous.title: Arrow billing overcharge and unsynced linked licenses fixed
since_previous.description: Arrow billing could overcharge because line totals were billed more than once, and licenses linked to resources were not synced. Line totals are now billed once and linked licenses are synced. Historical consumption is now looked up by the Arrow license rather than the resource backend_id.

actions.description: Apply waldur_arrow migration 0008_bill_arrow_line_totals_once.

since_previous.title: Arrow bills each license-month once and never changes issued invoices
since_previous.description: Previously, Arrow consumption could reach invoices from more than one billing source and could change invoices that were already issued. Now, each Arrow license-month is billed exactly once, issued invoices are never changed, and adjustment items are named after the month they correct.

actions.description: Apply waldur_arrow migration 0009_single_arrow_billing_source.

since_previous.title: Arrow integration no longer exposes the Arrow API key
since_previous.description: The Arrow integration exposed the Arrow API key. This release fixes that exposure.

security.affected_versions: Waldur versions before 8.1.5-rc.4 that run the Arrow integration
security.exploitability: The commit data does not describe how the key was exposed or who could read it.
security.mitigation: Upgrade to 8.1.5-rc.4. Consider rotating the Arrow API key.

actions.description: Consider rotating the Arrow API key configured in Waldur.

since_previous.title: Call event feed hidden from reviewers and panel members
since_previous.description: A call's reviewers and panel members could see the call's event feed. The feed is now hidden from them.

since_previous.title: Call managers can message the reviewers of selected proposals
since_previous.description: Previously, call managers could not message the reviewers of selected proposals from Waldur. Now, they can, and a new event type and notification template support it.

since_previous.title: Category sections and attributes editable from the Categories admin page
since_previous.description: Previously, editing category sections and attributes through the API could lose data, and the admin UI had no editor for them. Now, sections and attributes can be edited through the API without data loss, and from the Categories admin page. Public offering pages render the updated sections and attributes.

since_previous.title: Clearing fields in update dialogs takes effect
